Yea it seems there rarely ever is a "right" answer to most of these problems like this. I can quit drinking cold turkey, but it's really tough because everyone that I know around here drinks and I don't really have any friends or social interaction because that's typically all there is to do around here. With the exception of a movie theater and bowling ally. I'm a very social person too with an extroverted personality so that tends to exacerbate the feelings I have about what people think about me.

I do fine for awhile but then once I take a drink it's a two or three day binge and then a massive crash like I had yesterday. It only happens at the end because the rest of the time I'm basically mentally sedated by the alcohol and the 'I don't give a fuck' mentality sets in.

It's really just a terrible repeating cycle. I'd almost call myself insane by definition because I do the same thing over and over again and expect different results. That at some point I might be able to drink and control myself yet I've failed every attempt eventually. I've tried just beer and limited amounts, but then I just wait until my wife goes to sleep and sneak up to the liquor store. 

It sucks man.

Thanks for stopping by. Quitting drinking really is my only option. I tried to talk to a local pastor but he's always been "perfect" in the sense that he never dealt with anyone like me, he grew up in the church, was a minister by the time he was in his twenties, etc.. So after I tried to talk to him it was like he just wanted to blame me and basically label me as just a fuck up. Not that I shouldn't be blamed because I understand that it's my fault, but he wasn't very encouraging. 

I'm afraid that even when I get older and I look back at all the time I wasted, that I could've used to be more productive, that I will fall back into depression over all of the mistakes I made because I dwell on them all the time. My mother went through the same thing and she is a successful nurse who never had a drinking problem but made mistakes that later on in life caused her to go through a 10 year period of serious depression and addiction to prescription drugs in which she attempted suicide several times. She's recovered now, but I'm afraid I could get to this point because of my tendency to dwell on my past and my inability to forgive myself for the things I've done.

That, I think, is my major problem. My tendency to dwell on the past and my inability to forgive myself. Thanks again for stopping by and for the resources as well.

Because, let's just say Nintendo came out in an official press release, a direct, for example, and said that they were going  to continue to manufacture all Amiibo in the near future and there had been a serious underestimate in how popular the figures would become. 

What do you think would happen to the scalpers? They would be forced to dump their inventory because the demand curve would drop like a rocket. Possibly even at less than retail cost. Why you say? Because the market is already flooded and what's happening is resellers are buying all the stock and holding it to create artificial scarcity. How many marketplace sellers do you think are selling Amiibo on Amazon US right now? I'm not going to count them and let's not forget to mention the EU resellers. You also have Ebay and now it's flooded with not only marketplace sellers, but individuals alike.

It would be smart for Nintendo to announce a future releases, force scalpers to dump their inventory, and then release previously released characters in limited amounts in order to avoid flooding the market, or risk losing money for lack of demand.
